keyboard.behavior: Follow native navigation links and the authored focus stop on the scrolling region.
Navigate to a real fragment; smooth mode also settles the URL and destination focus.

keyboard.keys: Arrow keys / Page Up / Page Down
keyboard.behavior: Scroll the focused region using native browser behavior, not a custom Scrollspy keyboard controller.

guidelines: Use unique IDs and real fragment links scoped to visible sections inside the observed element.
The activation line defaults to topMargin=12%; gaps retain the last active section and the bottom sentinel selects the last section.
rootMargin overrides topMargin; topMargin pixel values trigger a debounced observer rebuild on resize.
Call refresh after inserting/reordering sections or revealing an initially hidden container. Hidden targets are ignored at initialization.
Only active classes are managed; aria-current is not automatically added or updated. If your application supplies it, keep it synchronized yourself.
Smooth navigation replaces the hash without adding a history entry and focuses the section after settling; passive scroll activation does not move focus.
Scrollspy has no dedicated Sass partial or component token map. Configure the Nav/List group presentation instead.

keyboard.behavior: Follow native actions; an initialized toast pauses autohide while it has keyboard focus.
Activate a focused native button. Links use Enter for ordinary navigation.

guidelines: Toasts are opt-in: construct/get an instance and call show explicitly. data-trm-dismiss="toast" supplies dismissal, not automatic showing.
Create the live region before inserting/updating a notification. Static page examples do not prove a screen reader announced a live update.
Use polite status for routine feedback and assertive alert only for urgent information; retain persistent alternatives.
autohide defaults to true with delay=5000ms. Initialized instances pause during hover/focus and schedule a full delay after interaction leaves.
Persistent/actionable notifications need autohide=false and named dismissal controls. Applications decide where focus goes if a focused toast is hidden.
show/hide starts are cancelable; shown/hidden occur after the CSS callback. Hiding keeps the node; dispose clears the timer and instance.
Use toast-instant to skip transitions; there is no animation option, showing class or separate hide class in this pin.
